Definition: drought; also a cutting instrument (from its destructive effect), as a knife, sword, or other sharp implement
BiblicalUsage: Chereb is the sword, the cutting blade that stands for war, judgment and God's own word of power throughout the Old Testament. A flaming sword guards the way to the tree of life, Moses commands the Levites to take the sword through the camp, the captain of the Lord's host meets Joshua with a drawn sword, and David faces Goliath trusting not in a sword but in the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the sword in Scripture always asks whose side we are on, because the same blade can defend or destroy. I hold that God's sword cuts true, and that is why David's trust was in the Lord and not in his own weapon.
